evidence.interpretation: Source observation: missing Cache-Control retains false and explicit directive matching uses a private set. The old isCached method remains as a deprecated forwarding method after the more precise rename.

Source observation: the retained negative assertion forbids adding the cookie to this shared-cache response. Neighboring tests cover absent headers, private, no-store, capitalization and spaces, with GET/non-GET distinctions.

Source observation: the private decision helper separates All with credentials, All without credentials, explicit matches, wildcard fallbacks, and rejection. It cannot be replaced by one allow-all boolean without changing semantics.

Source observation: response-header assertions cover wildcard behavior; new tests also cover an explicit origin taking priority over wildcard. These are server-side assertions and do not constitute browser credential-enforcement testing.

Source observation: the 2020 build separates core, web filters, transport backends, testkit and dev tooling. The actual sbt project ID is Filters-Helpers, not the Scala val name; integration tests are in IntegrationTest, and scripted support is another test layer.

Source observation: the 2022 integration project still uses IntegrationTest with non-publication and both Akka HTTP and Netty dependencies. A 2024 Test selector cannot simply be applied to this snapshot.

Source observation: by December 2024 the filter ID has the Play prefix; the integration project uses Test and Pekko HTTP replaces Akka HTTP in this tree. Run support is a non-cross-built Java boundary, and Play-Configuration is separated from Play core.

Source observation: the December 2020 snapshot pins Akka HTTP 10.1.13 and defaults Akka to 2.6.10. These are snapshot defaults, not assertions about the January 2020 PR head or every Play 2.8 release.

Source observation: the December 2022 snapshot defaults Akka HTTP to 10.2.10 and Akka to 2.6.20, with system-property overrides. This is a JVM Future/Akka Streams line rather than an effect-polymorphic migration.

Source observation: the 2024 tree declares runtime-era Scala 2.13.15 and Scala 3.3.4 versions alongside Scala 2.12.20 for sbt-related work. Exact supported cross-build membership still depends on each project plugin.

Source observation: the December 2024 tree defaults Pekko to 1.0.3 and Pekko HTTP to 1.0.1. Porting a historical Akka snippet requires resolving this namespace and dependency boundary, not a blind current-source substitution.

claims.rule: Before changing CORS or CSRF configuration matching, write a behavior matrix for missing values, explicit wildcards, specific origins, credentials and shared-cache directives, and retain legacy cases separately from intended behavior changes.
claims.applicability: Historical 2018-2020 review guidance for Play web filters. Preserving historical defaults during a compatibility fix is different from recommending permissive defaults for new deployments. Current-version checks must confirm browser semantics and the application threat model.
claims.counterexample: An explicitly approved security migration may intentionally tighten an unsafe default. It should document the migration and expected breakage rather than disguise it as a behavior-preserving refactor.

claims.rule: Keep a filter decision helper at the visibility required by its callers and avoid combining a semantic repair with an unrelated cache-header optimization; identify which header values and missing-value cases remain unchanged.
claims.applicability: Observed scoped review in PR 10146 and source evidence of a deprecated forwarding method in PR 8363. This is more specific than a blanket preference for private code: public extensions and compatibility bridges must remain accessible.
claims.counterexample: An existing documented extension point used by applications cannot be narrowed solely because its implementation looks internal; usages and release policy govern that decision.

claims.rule: Before validating a Play filter policy change, resolve the actual filter project ID, concrete CORS consumers and integration configuration; do not count a shared trait selector or an outdated project name as executed regression coverage.
claims.applicability: Inference from pinned builds and test sources: Filters-Helpers becomes Play-Filters-Helpers, IntegrationTest becomes Test, and CORSCommonSpec is a trait. Resolve inherited compiler defaults and property overrides without treating meta-build Scala as the runtime compiler.
claims.counterexample: A testOnly command that discovers zero concrete CORS tests does not validate origin policy even if sbt exits successfully; source inspection alone does not establish runtime or browser enforcement.
